There are three Duke Power Company electric power generating stations in the Keowee Valley: Jocassee Pumped Storage, Keowee Hydro, and Oconee Nuclear Station. The nearest generating station, Jocassee, 7 miles southeast of the proposed project, has one transmission line extending south to the Oconee Nuclear Station, one line extending east to Pickens, and a line extending east to the Shiloh Tie Station. These lines are above ground.
Oconee Nuclear Station, 17 miles south-southeast of the proposed project, apart from having the above-mentioned ties with Jocassee, has one line extending northeast to McGuire Switching Station in North Carolina, one line extending east to North Greenville, one line extending southeast to York, three lines extending southeast to Central, South Carolina, and a line extending south to Newry, South Carolina. The Keowee Hydro Station has one transmission line connected with the Oconee Nuclear Station. Applicant's transmission system is shown in Figure 1-2.
2.1.2 Recreation
Present outdoor recreation in the immediate project area is confined to dispersed activities such as hunting, fishing, primitive camping, sightseeing, hiking, and offroad motor vehicle use. This type of use results from a lack of user facilities and very difficult access due to steep slopes and often dense vegetation.
Highway 107, extending north-south, is located about 2 miles west, and provides good access to the project area via Highway 413, extending east-west. Another north-south road, Highway 171, skirts the western boundary of the project, intersecting with Highway 413. A more distant major north-south access route, Highway 178, is located about 12 miles east of the project area and would intersect with the proposed hiking trail.
Although the project would be located within the proclamation boundary of the Sumter National Forest, no project lands would be administered by the Forest Service. The Keowee Unit of the Sumter National Forest is located about 4 miles west of the project, while the Whitewater River Unit of the Nantahala National Forest is located immediately north in the State of North Carolina. Public outdoor recreation facilities in the Keowee Unit include 3 picnic areas, a camping area (25 units), over 18 miles of hiking trails, and 2 overlooks (U.S. Forest Service, 1974a).
